## Iterative consensus picks

Our current method for determining the consensus picks among our zooniverse classfications applies code to the entire dataset, which can make error checking rather problematic.

Here I am writing new code (April, Nov 2026) that will work through the data one deployment at a time to assign the consensus choice for each subject_id.

This code assumes that you have a Flattened file in your environment with both annotations and subject_data parsed from the downloaded zooniverse classification file.

## Overview

Once we have flattened all of our data, we need to examine it to determine the consensus species ID for each event.

We need to know the following:

- For how many subject ids were all of the choices the same (i.e. all classifiers identified the same species)?

- What was the chosen species for each of these subject ids?

- For which subject_ids were there discrepancies in what the species_id was?

- How many of these subject_ids were there?

- For which subject_ids were there more than one species present in the set of photos?

We'll see below that these are the cases in which num_votes is greater than num_class

- Are there discrepancies in what species are indicated as present? How will we reconcile them?

- Can we keep data on what percent of IDs were problematic?

### Set up

```{r}
#rm(list = ls()) #uncomment if starting fresh
library(tidyverse)
library(googledrive) # to connect to, read and write csv files stored on google
library(googlesheets4) #to read a googlesheet in as .csv
library(pander)
library(here)
```

### Read in flattened file

If you are not continuing from an earlier script with data already in your environment, you will need to read in a `flattened` file:

#### Option A - CSV file stored on google

Step 1. Link to file stored on google drive

```{r}
file_id <- "https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Tm7WiXdknLmmWbPmIv_HRFQYSTFMS30K/view?usp=drive_link"
```

Step 2 - get file info from googledrive

```{r}
flat_file <- drive_get(file_id) #pulls info from google drive for the file
flat_file$name #prints file name - check to make sure you have pulled correct file
```

Step 3 - read file

```{r}
Flattened <- read_csv(drive_read_string(flat_file))
```

#### Option B - Read directly from a google sheet (not saved as .csv)

```{r}
Flattened <- read_sheet("https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1BOhUKaEgA_SBqcY5-1pQn0K4DWbebujMcA5R0G-3m6k/edit?usp=sharing", col_names = TRUE)
```

## Prep the file

Check to see that there is a column called `newDTO_img1` in the file

```{r}
"newDTO_img1" %in% names(Flattened)
```

If there is not, use the code below to fix the dates.

### Fix Dates

One thing we should do for determining consensus picks is to correct the dates associated with the date-time of the first image in each subject set.

```{r}
# Flattened <- Flattened |>
#   mutate(
#     newDTO_img1 = parse_date_time(DTO_Img1, c("mdy_HM", "ymd_HMS", "ymd")))
#     
# Flattened <- Flattened |>
#   relocate(newDTO_img1, .after = DTO_Img1)

#Nov 2026 file has column called subject.DateTimeOriginal_Img1 for which 19% of dataset is NA

Flattened <- Flattened |>
  mutate(
    newDTO_img1 = parse_date_time(subject.DateTimeOriginal_Img1, c("mdy_HM", "ymd_HMS", "ymd"))
  ) |>
  relocate(newDTO_img1, .before = subject.DateTimeOriginal_Img1)
```

### Delete empty columns

Next, check to see if there area any empty columns in dataset and delete if there are. You don't need to do this if you are coming directly from `3.Flatten_Species_IDs.Rmd`

But if you have some, get rid of any empty columns in the dataset:

```{r}
empty_cols <- sapply(Flattened, function(x)all(is.na(x))) #identify the columns that only contain NA
dump <- which(empty_cols == TRUE)

Flattened <- Flattened |>
  select(!(all_of(dump)))
```

### Get rid of answers to questions

Now let's get rid of the columns that begin with `answers.` to clean up the data a bit. We may want these at some point if we try to look at behavior.

```{r}
Flattened <- Flattened |>
  select(!starts_with("answers"))
```

### Combine cottontail and snowshoe hare

```{r}
Flattened <- Flattened |>
  mutate(modified_choice = choice) |>
  relocate(modified_choice, .after = choice)

Flattened <- Flattened |>
  mutate(
    modified_choice = replace_when(modified_choice, choice == "COTTONTAILRABBIT" | choice == "SNOWSHOEHARE" ~ "RABBIT OR HARE")
  )
```

Get rid of beta test classifications

Let's get rid of the data from the zooniverse beta test

```{r}
beta <- Flattened |>
  filter(deploy_round == "beta test")

#remove them from data
to_remove <- which(Flattened$deploy_round == "beta test")

Flattened <- Flattened[-to_remove,]

unique(Flattened$deploy_round)

```

Get rid of duplicate columns. When we flattened the file, we ended up with repeat user_name, subject_ids, workflow_name and workflow_version columns. Fix

```{r}
#drop .y versions
dump <- c("subject_ids.y", "user_name.y", "workflow_name.y", "workflow_version.y")
Flattened <- Flattened |>
  select(-all_of(dump))
#now rename existing

Flattened <- Flattened |>
  rename(
    subject_ids = subject_ids.x,
    user_name = user_name.x,
    workflow_name = workflow_name.x,
    workflow_version = workflow_version.x
  )
```

### Clean up missing camera and sd card numbers in Flattened

Let's try to clean up the cam_sd combo

```{r}
#find those rows in which some part of cam_sd includes NA

Flattened |>
  filter(is.na(cam_number) | is.na(sd_number)) |>
 nrow() 

#now get their rows
cam_sd_na <- which(is.na(Flattened$cam_number) | is.na(Flattened$sd_number))

#now grab them 
fix_cam_sd <- Flattened |>
  filter(is.na(cam_number) | is.na(sd_number))

#now extract cam number, sd number

fix_cam_sd <- fix_cam_sd |>
  mutate(cam_number = as.character(as.integer(str_sub(image_1, 1,2))),
         sd_number = as.character(as.integer(str_sub(image_1, 4,5))),
         #create well-formatted camera number
         formatted_cam_number = 
           case_when(
             str_starts(cam_number, "C") ~ cam_number,
             as.numeric(cam_number) < 10 ~ paste0("C00", cam_number),
             as.numeric(cam_number) < 100 ~ paste0("C0", cam_number),
             TRUE ~ paste0("C", cam_number)),
         formatted_sd_number = 
           case_when(
             str_starts(sd_number, "SD") ~ sd_number,
             as.numeric(sd_number) < 10 ~ paste0 ("SD00", sd_number),
             as.numeric(sd_number) < 100 ~paste0("SD0", sd_number),
             TRUE ~ paste0("SD", sd_number)),
         cam_sd = paste0(formatted_cam_number, "_", formatted_sd_number)
         )

#now replace into Flattened

Flattened[cam_sd_na,] <- fix_cam_sd

#now check for nas in cam, sd card
Flattened |>
  filter(is.na(cam_number) | is.na(sd_number)) |>
 nrow() 

```

## Join to deployment data

Now read in the deployment data from google drive and join it to the classification data

### Get deployment data

#### Option 1. Read csv stored on google drive

Step 1. Set file path

```{r}
deployment_file <- "https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1BOhUKaEgA_SBqcY5-1pQn0K4DWbebujMcA5R0G-3m6k/edit?usp=sharing"

#Main deployment spreadsheet

```

Step 2. Get file info from google drive

```{r}
deploy_file <- drive_get(deployment_file) #pulls info from google drive for the file
deploy_file$name
```

Step 3. Read file.

```{r}
deployments <- read_csv(I(drive_read_string(deploy_file)))
```

#### Option 2. Read from google sheet (no csv)

```{r}
deployments <- read_sheet("https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1BOhUKaEgA_SBqcY5-1pQn0K4DWbebujMcA5R0G-3m6k/edit?usp=sharing")
```

NOTE: Dates should come in as POSIXct and no columns should come in as lists. If they do, need to go check structure of google sheet or fix after import.

### Clean up deployments file

May need some of these code chunks and not others depending on how your deployments file is structured on import.

Fix file error in column name

```{r}
#may not need this code; depends on format of deployment sheet you brought in
deployments <- deployments |>
  rename(deployment_date_standardized = deployment_data_standardized)
```

#### Get rid of unnecessary columns

```{r}
cols_to_drop <- c("project_lead", "other_students","camera_trappers", "project_trap_code", "camera_brand", "camera_model", "round", "phase", "HEXID", "northing", "easting", "AM_present", "Num_AM_present", "AM_deployment_num", "gps_source", "gps_accuracy_m", "bushnell_bat_start_bars", "bushnell_bat_end_bars", "battery_percent_start", "battery_percent_end", "lithium_or_recharge", "tem_logger_num", "snowstake_distance_m", "cam_orientation_degrees", "cam_orientation_string", "tree_species")

deployments <- deployments |>
  select(-all_of(cols_to_drop))

summary(deployments)
```

#### Get rid of video deployments

Since we are matching zooniverse data, which is only images and no video, with our deployments, we can omit from deployments those instances in which media_type is video. For now, keep "images & video"

```{r}
unique(deployments$media_type)

deployments <- deployments |>
  filter(media_type != "video")
```

#### Assign date fields

```{r}
deployments <- deployments |>
  mutate(
    deployment_date_standardized = dmy(deployment_date_standardized),
    collection_date_standardized = dmy(collection_date_standardized)
  )

summary(deployments$deployment_date_standardized)
summary(deployments$collection_date_standardized)
```

There are some deployments for which no one recorded the collection date, so we don't have it. Let's get a list so we can re-check data sheets or use date of last image to assess.

```{r}
deployments |>
  filter(is.na(collection_date_standardized)) |>
  select(deployment_number) |>
  pander()
```

### Compare columns between Flattened and deployments

#### Check the primary keys

We should verify that the primary keys in each table (cam_sd in Flattened and Cam_SD in deployments) uniquely identify each observation. We can use `count()` and look for entries where `n > 1`

```{r}
Flattened |>
  count(cam_sd) |>
  filter(n >1) |>
  pander()
```

In `Flattened`, there are many rows in which cam_sd repeats, which makes sense, because we have multiple `subject_ids` from each deployment.

What about in deployments?

```{r}
deployments |>
  count(Cam_SD) |>
  filter(n > 1) |>
  pander()
```

There are 18 rows in which Cam_SD is repeated. This is a problem, because we reused Cam_SD card combinations. So we don't know which Cam_SD of those 19 rows is the proper match in `Flattened`. Let's take a look at those

```{r}
check <- deployments |>
  count(Cam_SD) |>
  filter(n > 1) 
```

Now filter just those deployments

```{r}
deployments |> 
  filter(Cam_SD %in% check$Cam_SD) |>
  arrange(Cam_SD, deployment_date) |>
  View()
```

We could perhaps have a `surrogate` primary key that combines Cam_SD with deployment number.

```{r}
deployments |>
  count(Cam_SD, deployment_number) |>
  filter(n > 1) |>
  pander()
```

Or a surrogate primary key that uses deployment_date

```{r}
deployments |>
  count(Cam_SD, deployment_date) |>
  filter(n > 1) |>
  pander()
```

There are no cases with repeats for either combination, so each combination gives a unique id.

### Check for many-to-many relationships

To do a join, we'd like to know what camera_sd combinations are common between the 2 datasets

```{r}
common_cams <- intersect(Flattened$cam_sd, deployments$Cam_SD)
```

Now look to see if there are camera_sd combinations that are not shared between the 2 datasets

```{r}
Flat_v_deploy <- setdiff(Flattened$cam_sd, deployments$Cam_SD)
```

There are no cameras in Flattened that are not in deployments;

Are there cameras in deployments that are not in Flattened?

```{r}
deploy_v_Flat <- setdiff(deployments$Cam_SD, Flattened$cam_sd)
```

There are 111 cameras in deployments that do not occur in Flattened.

Let's look at them.

Let's remove them.

```{r}
deployments |>
  filter(Cam_SD %in% deploy_v_Flat) |>
  View()
```

According to the deployments sheet, these deployments have not been uploaded to the zooniverse. That would be good to check. Let's write that list of deployments.

```{r}
write_csv(filter(deployments, Cam_SD %in% deploy_v_Flat), "/Users/ebar/Desktop/not_on_zooniverse.csv")
```
That also seems like a LOT of deployments, so I wonder if some of them are present in the "Is there an animal" workflow but that didn't get to this workflow?


#STOPPED HERE

```{r}
#create function to negate %in%
`%nin%` <- Negate(`%in%`) #that's the function
deployments_small <- deployments |>
  filter(Cam_SD %nin% deploy_v_Flat)
```

Reduced deployments to 140. Now see if Cam_SD is unique

```{r}
deployments_small |>
  count(Cam_SD) |>
  filter(n > 1) |>
  pander()
```

Now there are 11 Cam_SD combinations in deployments_small that are repeated.

Let's look at them:

```{r}
deployments_small |>
  count(Cam_SD, deployment_data_standardized) |>
  filter(n > 1) |>
  pander()
```

Isolate them

```{r}
check1 <- deployments_small |>
  count(Cam_SD) |>
  filter(n > 1) 
```

Now view just those deployments that repeat

```{r}
deployments_small |> 
  filter(Cam_SD %in% check1$Cam_SD) |>
  arrange(Cam_SD, deployment_data_standardized) |>
  View()
```

And now let's look at the Flattened data for those cams

```{r}
Flattened |>
  filter(CamSD %in% check1$Cam_SD) |>
  arrange(CamSD, newDTO_img1) |>
  View()
```

### Join the datasets

It looks like we have an unfortunate case in which the Cam_SD field has repeated instances representing DIFFERENT deployments.So I think I need to do a fancy join in which I check that the newDTOimage1 in Flattened falls within the deployment date and collection date in deployments.

First, let's make sure that for any given Cam_SD in deployments, there is no overlap in deployment dates (which should be impossible):

```{r}
deployments_small |> 
  arrange(Cam_SD, deployment_data_standardized) |>
  group_by(Cam_SD) |>
  mutate(
    overlap = deployment_data_standardized <=lag(collection_date_standardized) 
  ) |>
  filter(overlap)
```

There are zero rows, so it seems no overlap.

Next, we'll try a fancy join, something like:

result \<- left_join( Flattened, deployments_small, join_by( CamSD == Cam_SD, newDTO_img1 \>= deployment_data_standardized, newDTO_img1 \<= collection_date_standardized ) )

Let's try it!

```{r}
test_join <- left_join(
  Flattened, 
  deployments_small,
  join_by(
    CamSD == Cam_SD,
    newDTO_img1 >= deployment_data_standardized,
    newDTO_img1 <= collection_date_standardized
    )
)
```

Are there any subject_ids in test_join for which deployment_id is na?

```{r}
  length(which(is.na(test_join$deployment_number)))
```

Ok - there are 1650 rows for which the join didn't work. Let's take a look at them

```{r}
test_join |>
  filter(is.na(deployment_number)) |>
  View()
```

now figure out what cameras they are from

```{r}
join_prob <- test_join |>
  filter(is.na(deployment_number))

prob_cams <- unique(join_prob$CamSD)
prob_cams
```

Now look at those cams in deployments

```{r}
deployments_small|>
  filter(Cam_SD %in% prob_cams) |>
  View()
```

I think it worked! Now get rid of all empty columns!

```{r}
empty_cols <- sapply(test_join, function(x)all(is.na(x))) #identify the columns that only contain NA
dump <- which(empty_cols == TRUE)

test_join <- test_join |>
  select(!dump)
```
